Description: Total sample size across both clinical/trait and control groups included in the final analysis.
Example values: Integer count (e.g., 48, 71)

Description: Number of participants categorized into the ADHD or high-trait ADHD experimental group.
Example values: Integer count or subtype breakdown (e.g., 24, 53, 40 (18 inattentive; 22 combined))

Description: Proportion of female individuals within the ADHD / trait cohort.
Example values: Numeric value (0–1) or NA

Description: Mean age (in years) of the ADHD / trait cohort.
Example values: Numeric (mean in years) or NA

Description: Standard deviation of participant age in the ADHD / trait cohort.
Example values: Numeric (SD in years) or NA

Description: Proportion of female individuals within the healthy comparison/control group.
Example values: Numeric value (0–1) or NA

Description: Mean age (in years) of the healthy comparison/control group.
Example values: Numeric (mean in years) or NA

Description: Standard deviation of age in the healthy comparison/control group.
Example values: Numeric (SD in years) or NA

Description: Explanations for missing values given by authors (if any)
Example values: Long String or blank

Description: Indicates whether the study employed group-level matching (e.g., age, sex, IQ) between ADHD and control groups at design/recruitment stage.
Example values: 1 = Matched at group level; 0 = Not matched / unstated / single group

Description: Qualitative description of design-stage procedures or justification used to manage age differences between cohorts.
Example values: Narrative summary (e.g., 'None: Relying purely on baseline matching; no age covariates in final models')

Description: Indicates whether participant age was formally modeled as a covariate in downstream statistical analyses.
Example values: 1 = Statistically controlled/covaried; 0 = Not statistically controlled

Description: Qualitative protocol detailing how stimulant medication was handled prior to behavioral/EEG testing.
Example values: Narrative detail (e.g., 'Washout: 48 hours prior to recording', 'Stimulant-Naïve', 'Unmedicated')

Description: Binary indicator for whether an explicit stimulant control procedure was enforced.
Example values: 1 = Procedural control enforced (washout, medication-naïve cohort); 0 = No explicit stimulant control / unmedicated status unverified

Description: Qualitative report of active non-stimulant psychoactive medications (e.g., SSRIs, atomoxetine, anticonvulsants) present or permitted in the ADHD group.
Example values: Narrative inventory of concurrent medications or confirmation of none active

Description: Binary indicator evaluating whether the ADHD cohort was completely free from concurrent non-stimulant psychoactive medications during testing.
Example values: 1 = Verified free from other psychoactive medications; 0 = Other psychoactive medications present or permitted

Description: Qualitative narrative describing the broader methodological or analytical strategy used to account for medication confounding.
Example values: Narrative summary (e.g., 'Exclusion/Washout: ≥ 6 half-lives', 'None: Flagged as methodological limitation')

Description: Indicates whether medication (especially stimulants) status (or dose/class) was included as a covariate or factor in downstream statistical models.
Example values: 1 = Statistically controlled; 0 = Not statistically controlled; NA = Not applicable (e.g., medication-free cohort)

Description: Classification of the target ADHD population examined.
Example values: Categorical: 'clinical' (formal DSM/ICD diagnosis), 'ADHD-traits' (dimensional/subclinical cohort), or hybrid

Description: Criteria and reporting regarding co-occurring psychiatric or neurological conditions in the study cohort.
Example values: Narrative summary (e.g., 'None (pure ADHD cohort)', 'Psychiatric comorbidities permitted unless primary acute treatment was required')

Description: Inventory of specific diagnostic interviews, psychometric dimensional scales, or screening tools administered.
Example values: Specific instrument names/acronyms (e.g., DIVA, CAARS, ASRS, BADDS, WURS)

Description: Quality rating assessing the depth of ADHD diagnostic operationalization based on three core components: (1) clinical interview, (2) dimensional ADHD questionnaire, and (3) retrospective childhood symptom assessment.
Example values: A = All 3 core components present; B = At least one standardized dimensional scale (e.g., CAARS) or structured clinical interview; C = Relies solely on screening tools or checklists

Description: Indicates whether the study explicitly conducted statistical analyses testing the relationship between behavioral/EEG parameters and dimensional ADHD symptom scales.
Example values: yes' = Dimensional brain/behavior vs. symptom relationship statistically modeled; 'no' = Between-group comparisons only without continuous symptom correlation
